purpose: Ingest security and algorithmic findings surfaced by sparse states 39441, 34194, 14449 and 14944, emphasizing authorization, TLS trust, GPU memory semantics, privileged file handling, parser robustness, CI/plugin output encoding, CMS controls, package registries and dispatch optimization.

source_ingestion_policy.rule: Every substantive unique publication, dataset, advisory, standard, algorithmic method or information item receives a Worldshepherd use when it materially improves any capability, or an explicit negative-control role.
source_ingestion_policy.duplicates: NVD/CNA/vendor mirrors and article-index copies for the same underlying source are provenance aliases and are not independent evidence.
source_ingestion_policy.search_noise: CVE IDs and article numbers can materially improve Worldshepherd security/operations methodology but carry zero automatic Glob evidence and never become P1/P2 solely from recurrence.

sources.title: CVE-2024-39441 — Wi-Fi display missing permission check
sources.note: Use as a local peripheral/display authorization test: media/sensing paths require explicit permission checks independent of caller expectations. 39441 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2023-39441 — Apache Airflow certificate validation failure
sources.note: Use as a TLS trust-boundary test: encrypted transport without peer certificate validation is insufficient. 39441 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: Optimization of a comprehensive dispatching system based on ant colony algorithm and dynamic weight power dispatching strategy
sources.note: Use ant-colony search plus dynamic-weight scheduling as an operations-optimization reference for resource dispatch experiments. 39441 is the article number.

sources.title: CVE-2026-34194 — Imagination GPU sparse-memory mapping defect
sources.note: Use as a dimensional/address-arithmetic test case: implicit scaling across differently sized buffers can create wrong-memory references in sparse allocations. 34194 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2025-34194 — privileged temp-file/symlink handling in Vasion Print
sources.note: Use as a privileged-service filesystem test: never create privileged files inside user-controlled temporary directories without link-safe semantics. 34194 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2023-34194 — TinyXML reachable assertion
sources.note: Use crafted-document/parser fuzzing as a robustness case for XML and other structured-data ingestion. 34194 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2022-34194 — Jenkins Readonly Parameter Plugin stored XSS
sources.note: Use as a CI/automation UI output-encoding case: even supposedly readonly metadata must be escaped in every rendering context. 34194 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2026-14449 — u5CMS reflected XSS
sources.note: Use context-aware input/output handling for reflected parameters as a web-interface test case. 14449 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2025-14449 — Backup Migration missing authorization
sources.note: Use as an automation-control case: publicly visible tokens are not substitutes for server-side capability/nonce authorization. 14449 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2019-14944 — GitLab Gitaly command-line flag injection
sources.note: Use as a command-construction test: user-controlled repository/path values must not be interpreted as executable flags. 14944 is the CVE identifier.

sources.title: CVE-2017-14944 — ProGet dangerous package-ID handling
sources.note: Use as a package-registry namespace/input validation precedent. 14944 is the CVE identifier.

information_updates.finding: The cluster reinforces a common Worldshepherd security rule: validate semantics at the trust boundary, not merely syntax. Permission checks, certificate identity, path/link semantics, buffer/address scaling, parser termination, output encoding, capability checks and command-argument construction each fail when a lower-level representation is accepted without enforcing its intended meaning.
information_updates.claims_boundary: Engineering synthesis from unrelated CVEs; their shared five-digit targets do not imply a causal or numerical relation.

information_updates.finding: The 2025 dispatching study combines ant-colony optimization with dynamic weights, providing a candidate algorithmic comparison point for Worldshepherd scheduling/resource-allocation experiments where priorities change over time.
information_updates.claims_boundary: Candidate benchmark only; performance claims require reproduction on Worldshepherd workloads.

next_actions: Continue analyzer-driven sparse-state scans and reduce single-record/single-namespace counts.
Search the actual Worldshepherd repository/dependency inventory for Airflow, Jenkins, GitLab/Gitaly, ProGet, TinyXML and relevant GPU/print components before asserting exposure.
Evaluate dynamic-weight/ant-colony dispatching only against preregistered local workloads and baselines.
Continue same-system physical topology with fixed tolerance and experiment-wide multiple-testing/false-discovery controls.
